correctness.rationale: The theorem is equivalent to four Walsh scalar blocks and one \(2\times2\) quaternion block. Its determinant is the exact quadratic sum of differences, and the regular rank is \(K+2r\). The exhaustive scalar-support sets \(\mathcal K_0,\ldots,\mathcal K_4\), singular-block exclusions, and explicit constructions establish impossibility and existence for every one of 14 occupancy types. Standalone exact SymPy constructions verify 64 canonical row-rank witnesses; separately implemented eight-by-eight regular-matrix computations verify 1,148 instances across all 255 exact supports, with group associativity and all 24 Walsh coordinate permutations tested. This is a complete proof, not a finite-experiment extrapolation.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a natural exhaustive rank-weighted uncertainty diagram on the smallest nonabelian Hamiltonian group and quantifies the nontrivial dependence on antipodal support geometry. At the same cardinality, four- and six-point supports have genuinely different forbidden and attainable rank sets, determining which convolution maps have a given kernel dimension. Unlike a narrow arbitrary number, the invariant classifies every fixed support and rank and is directly motivated by nonabelian Fourier uncertainty and spectral invertibility. It does not claim broader-group or real-weight extensions.
